case_title.quote: Chotkau v. State of Uttar Pradesh
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment heading.

number_of_accused.quote: the sole accused has come up with the above appeals

accused_gender.quote: the appellant herein took his niece aged about 6 years
accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to with male pronouns throughout.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is described.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.reason: Accused's occupation is not stated; PW-2's remark concerns the accused's brothers only.

accused_socioeconomic_status.quote: this is a case where the appellant is so poor that he could not afford to engage a lawyer
accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Judgment expressly describes the appellant's poverty and need for amicus.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned in the judgment.

victim_gender.quote: a six year old girl had been raped and murdered
victim_gender.reason: Victim is a girl, so Female is supported.

victim_age.quote: a six year old girl had been raped and murdered
victim_age.reason: Victim's age of six is stated in the judgment.

victim_caste.reason: No caste or community of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religious identity of the victim is described.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Relative (niece, as stated in the prosecution complaint); land dispute and enmity between accused and Zalim Khan, a rival, described
accused_victim_relationship.quote: PW-6: I had detected that a land dispute was proceeding between accused Chotkau and Zalim Khan.
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Niece relationship is correct, but 'no prior enmity' is not stated by the court and the judgment describes a land dispute and rivalry.

offence_category.quote: charged for the commission of the offences of raping the minor girl and murdering her
offence_category.reason: Murder is a reasonable primary category given the charges of rape and murder.

statutory_provisions.quote: Convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code
statutory_provisions.reason: Sections 302 and 376 IPC are the charged provisions.

weapon.reason: No weapon is mentioned in the judgment.

evidence_type.quote: the prosecution of the appellant is based on circumstantial evidence
evidence_type.reason: Circumstantial, last-seen, post-mortem, recovery and missing medical evidence are all reflected.

confession.reason: No confession; the accused denied the charges under Section 313.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: it is one of the rarest of rare cases where a six year old girl had been raped and murdered
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Trial court's aggravating finding about the six-year-old victim and rape-murder is recorded.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating circumstances are noted by the courts.

trial_court_outcome.quote: the Sessions Court convicted the appellant for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 376 of the IPC and awarded death penalty
trial_court_outcome.reason: Conviction under ss.302 and 376 and death sentence match the judgment.

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court confirmed conviction and death sentence on reference and appeal.

final_outcome.quote: the appeals are allowed and the conviction and penalty are set aside
final_outcome.reason: Conviction and sentence set aside and accused released, which is an acquittal.

offence_finally_established.quote: the conviction and penalty are set aside
offence_finally_established.reason: No offence stands after the conviction was set aside.

imprisonment_type.quote: the conviction and penalty are set aside
imprisonment_type.reason: No sentence stands, so 'none' is correct.

imprisonment_years.reason: No fixed-term sentence stands; null is correct.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is imposed or mentioned.

neutral_facts.reason: Neutral summary of the incident and evidence; no names, court outcomes or wealth details are included.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the statutory punishment range for ss.302 or 376.

attempt_completion.reason: Victim was murdered and rape was alleged, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.quote: Blood was coming out of her urinal track, her clothes had torn up and she had died.
physical_harm.reason: Death and alleged rape are reflected; injuries are not described in detail.

number_of_offences.quote: Convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 376
number_of_offences.reason: Two sections charged and none upheld after the Supreme Court decision.

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is part of the offence.

premeditation_planning.reason: The judgment does not find premeditation or planning.

motive.reason: No motive for the accused is accepted or alleged by the prosecution; the land-dispute theory relates to false implication.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the evidence of PWs 1 to 3 are not trustworthy
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court accepted none of PWs 1 to 3's evidence and treated the missing medical examination as fatal.

witness_credibility.quote: These contradictions make the evidence of PWs 1 to 3 completely untrustworthy.
witness_credibility.reason: Court found PWs 1 to 3 untrustworthy and the lower courts had trivialised contradictions.

post_offence_conduct.reason: Absconding was relied on by lower courts and the Supreme Court did not accept the evidence supporting it.

trial_duration.reason: Offence, High Court and Supreme Court dates match; trial judgment date is not given.

legal_representation.quote: S. Nagamuthu, Sr. Adv., Ms. Shivani Misra ... for the Appellant. Ardhendumauli Kumar Prasad, AAG ... for the Respondent.
legal_representation.reason: Appellant and State counsel are correctly identified.

investigation_status.quote: not sent by the Investigation Officer but by the Deputy Superintendent of Police ... presumably along with the final report
investigation_status.reason: FIR, final report, trial, missing forensic report and no medical exam are all supported.

procedural_irregularity.quote: the delay of 5 days in transmitting the FIR to the jurisdictional court, especially in the facts and circumstances of this case was fatal
procedural_irregularity.reason: Covers FIR delay, unidentified courier, contradictions, and missing medical and forensic steps.

appeal_history.quote: the appeals are allowed and the conviction and penalty are set aside
appeal_history.reason: Outcomes at trial, High Court and Supreme Court are correctly stated.

prosecution_argument.quote: there are no reasons for PWs 1 to 3 to implicate the appellant
prosecution_argument.reason: Summarises the State's contentions on witnesses, FIR delay, s.313 and forensic evidence accurately.

defence_argument.quote: the evidence of PWs 1 to 3 is untrustworthy; that there was an unexplained delay of five days
defence_argument.reason: Accurately summarises the appellant's contentions in the Supreme Court as set out in paragraph 11.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the Court must keep in mind five golden principles or the panchsheel
legal_principle_applied.reason: Panchsheel test, s.157(1) creditworthiness and s.53A medical evidence principles are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116 ... Rajendra Pralhadrao Wasnik (2019) 12 SCC 460 – relied on.
precedent_relied_upon.reason: All nine relied-on precedents and citations match the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.reason: No sentence is imposed, so 'Not applicable' is correct.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The court weighed no mitigating factors for sentencing.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The court weighed no aggravating factors for sentencing.

other_sentence_order.quote: The appellant shall be released forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case.
